title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement: Given two strings, return the length of their **longest common subsequence**: the longest sequence of characters that appears in both strings in the same order (the characters do not have to be next to each other). Return 0 if there is none.
idea: Solve it for short prefixes first and build up: `dp[i][j]` = answer for the first `i` letters of text1 and the first `j` letters of text2.
If the two current letters **match**, that letter extends the best answer of both shorter prefixes: `1 + diagonal`.
If they **differ**, at least one of them is unused: take the better of *drop text1's letter* (cell above) and *drop text2's letter* (cell to the left).

complexity.timeWhy: One table cell per pair of prefixes, each filled in O(1).

steps.text: Our example: **`text1 = "abcde", text2 = "ace"`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
Build a table with one extra row and column for the **empty prefix** (∅). An empty string has nothing in common with anything, so that row and column stay 0.

views.title: dp[i][j] = LCS of text1[:i] and text2[:j]

steps.text: `a` == `a` — a **match**. This letter can end the common subsequence, so take the best answer without both letters (diagonal: 0) and add 1 → **1**.
